World Food Programme
Pacific Multi-Country Office
OPERATIONAL CONTEXT
The Pacific Island Countries and Territories (PICTs) are
among the most hazard-prone in the world, with eight out
of the 20 nations experiencing the highest average disaster
losses in the world being in the Pacific. This situation is
further exacerbated by the global food crisis. Analysis
indicates that progress towards achieving the Sustainable
Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030 in PICTs has been
limited . This is in part driven by growing inequality, gender
inequity and public services that are insufficient to address
poverty, improve education or health outcomes; against
the backdrop of the climate crisis, food insecurity and
geopolitical pressures.
In July 2023, WFP started a Multi-Country Strategic Plan
(MCSP) 2023-2027, which is aligned with the 2050 Strategy
for the Blue Pacific Continent, the United Nations Pacific
Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (20232027) and the 14 country implementation plans that
represent the main strategic engagement between the
United Nations development system and Pacific
governments. WFP focuses on strengthening the capacities
of regional and national stakeholders for emergency
preparedness and response in logistics, emergency
telecommunications, disaster risk management, food
security and developing inclusive and accessible shockresponsive social protection systems that focus on those
most at risk of being left behind.
1

OVERVIEW OF OPERATIONS
PROVIDE SUPPORT TO STRENGTHEN SYSTEMS AND CAPACITIES
WFP’s work in the Pacific focuses on strengthening local,
national and regional capacities and systems to prepare
for, respond to, and recover from disasters and shocks. To
achieve this, WFP leverages its global expertise, tools and
partnership networks to support regional stakeholders,
especially the governments, in climate and disaster risk
management and response, in areas of logistics,
emergency telecommunications, food security and
nutrition – rather than directly distributing food or cash.
Supply Chain and Logistics: WFP supports
governments and regional partners in the Pacific to
prepare for emergencies and respond effectively by
offering technical and coordination support in logistics and
supply chain. WFP also supports 14 PICTs to understand
their current logistics capacity, needs and identifies gaps
through joint assessments. Additionally, WFP is partnering
with the University of the South Pacific to implement a
micro-accreditation programme for humanitarian supply
chain and logistics, aiming to enhance the skills and
knowledge of emergency responders.
Emergency Telecommunications (ETC): WFP
supports Pacific governments and regional partners to
strengthen emergency preparedness by providing
technical assistance and coordination support in
emergency telecommunications. WFP conducts ICT
capacity assessments across PICTs and produces
assessment reports as a supporting tool for national and
regional stakeholders. WFP then uses the assessment
results to identify regional capacity and establish an ETC
human resource register to facilitate the deployment of
qualified responders to the Pacific in emergency situations.
WFP also conducts national training and assessments to
strengthen capacity in the use of ETC equipment.
Food Security Monitoring: works with PICT
governments and partners to build national knowledge
bases through the generation of evidence-based
information. This informs effective policy formulation and
programming and minimises the impact of shocks and
disasters/ hazards on vulnerable communities. WFP works
in close collaboration with national counterparts in Fiji,
Kiribati, Samoa, Tonga and Vanuatu to collect crosssectional food security, nutrition and livelihoods data
through its remote mobile Vulnerability Analysis and
Mapping (mVAM) tool. WFP intends to expand the use of
this tool to the Solomon Islands and Tuvalu.
Cluster Coordination: WFP leads the regional Logistics
and Emergency Telecommunications Clusters of the Pacific
Humanitarian Team, and co-leads the regional Food
Security Cluster and the Pacific regional Cash Working
Group. WFP supports regional and national stakeholders to
reduce the risk of, prepare for, and respond to shocks
through its cluster work.
2 Date | Titre du fiche d’information

Anticipatory Action: WFP is working with the Fiji
Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection
(MWCSP) to implement an Anticipatory Action (AA) pilot
project in Fiji, funded by the UN Central Emergency
Response Fund (CERF), WFP and other partners. The AA
project aims to strengthen the Fiji government’s capacity to
deliver multi-purpose cash assistance to targeted social
welfare beneficiaries ahead of tropical cyclones. The AA
project will deliver cash assistance to up 15,000
beneficiaries through the MWCSP’s social protection
system.
Macro insurance: by partnering with the Pacific
Catastrophe Risk Insurance Company (PCRIC), WFP is
exploring ways to provide market-based disaster risk
financing solutions to help governments cover disaster
losses, thereby enabling faster, more cost-effective and
predictable responses to climate and disaster shocks.
Social Protection: WFP aims to help PICT governments
to scale-up and enhance social protection systems, as a key
pathway towards a more resilient Pacific region. WFP
works with governments and partners to ensure that by
2030, people will have substantially increased access to
national social protection systems that safeguard and
foster their ability to meet their food security, nutrition and
associated essential needs, and to manage the risks and
shocks they face.
Parametric micro insurance: WFP, WFP, in partnership
with the UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF),
supported MWCSP to pilot a climate risk insurance project
for 274 households following the Tropical Cyclone season
in 2021-2022. The project provided parametric insurance
to social welfare recipients living in high-disaster-risk
locations in Fiji through electronic cash transfers.
PROVIDE SERVICES UPON REQUEST
WFP provides on-demand services in response to suddenonset shocks upon request by government partners.
Examples of services that WFP has provided to Pacific
national and regional partners include:
Pacific Humanitarian Air Service: During COVID-19,
when the Pacific region was largely locked down, WFP
worked with the Pacific Islands Forum to run the Pacific
Humanitarian Air Service – a lifeline for PICTs, as it
transported humanitarian personnel and essential medical
cargo, when commercial flights had shut down. The Service
has been highlighted by national governments, regional
and development partners as a model for UN /
government partnerships in the Pacific.
Tonga volcanic eruption response: In response to the
Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha apai volcanic eruption and
tsunami in Tonga in January 2022 which disrupted air
travel and telecommunications in Tonga, WFP supported
the Government with logistics and re-established
connectivity to major swathes of the affected area. In the
same year, Kiribati was affected by a severe drought and
WFP supported the Government to monitor drought
impacts on food security through provision of equipment
and technical assistance.
Vanuatu TC Judy and Kevin response: In response of
the devastation caused by the category 4 tropical cyclones
Judy and Kevin in Vanuatu in March 2023, WFP transported
critical cargo by air and sea to provide essential medical
and food supplies to affected people. WFP also established
emergency telecommunications connectivity services,
enabling national and provincial emergency operation
centres to coordinate assistance, while providing remote
coordination and information management support.
Vanuatu TC Lola response: In response to the Tropical
Cyclone Lola in October 2023, WFP deployed supply chain
and logistics specialists to work with the Vanuatu National
Disaster Management Office (NDMO) to provide technical
assistance and provided necessary telecommunications
equipment requested by the Government to support
assessments. In addition, WFP provided technical
assistance to the national logistics cluster, led by NDMO
and WFP, to coordinate the logistics and response efforts
and facilitate timely response to affected populations living
in remote areas.
Photo credit: WFP/Kinley Wangmo
